newsitem.title: JORDAN: EU troika concerned by lack of Mideast progress.
newsitem.headline: EU troika concerned by lack of Mideast progress.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, leading a European Union troika visit to the Middle East, urged Israel and the Palestinians on Sunday to agree on a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Spring, arriving in Amman after talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad in Damascus, said the EU was concerned that Middle East peace talks were stalled.

"We want to see agreement being reached on the withdrawal of Israeli troops from Hebron," Spring told reporters at Amman airport. "We believe that would be a very important first step in getting momentum back into the peace process."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to modify the Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour government to safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes to the accord.
They hope to clinch a deal on the troop pullback during next week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo.

Spring said his talks in Damascus with Assad focused on Syrian-Israeli peace talks, suspended since the May election of Netanyahu, who rejects the principle of handing back occupied Arab lands for peace.
"We had a very useful exchange of views with President Assad in relation to the Syrian track and we discussed the prospects for the renewal of that," Spring told reporters.
But he said he was not mediating between Damascus and Israel. "We are not messengers between Syria and the Israelis."

The EU, the biggest donor of aid to the region and a major trading partner, feels it has been sidelined by the United States in efforts to get 1993 Middle East peace accords back on track, diplomats say.
It has appointed a special envoy to the region, Migual Moratinos, but stressed will complement, not compete with, Washington's efforts.

Spring, accompanied by envoys from the Netherland, Italy and EU, was due to meet Jordan's King Hussein in Amman. He would then fly to Gaza to meet Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat before travelling on to Egypt to see Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on the margins of the Cairo meeting.
Earlier plans for a visit to Jerusalem were cancelled after Israel objected to the EU's plans to visit Palestinians in Orient House in Arab East Jerusalem.
